title: African Technical Needs Survey: Analysis & Findings
content: When we started planning the WikiIndaba Hackathon 2026, we wanted to think about how to make the event as useful as possible for participants. Beyond the usual hackathon experience, we wanted people to get hands-on support, work together and, most importantly, spend time improving tools that African Wikimedia communities actually need. We didn’t want to make assumptions about what those needs were, so we decided to ask the community. Wiki Mentor Africa (WMA), on behalf of the hackathon planning committee, put together a Technical Needs Survey to find out which tools people currently use, what challenges they face and what they’d like to see improved.

title: We need to talk about being a good neighbor
content: Summary: Wikimedians depend on the valuable work of journalists, cultural heritage institutions, photographers and many volunteer contributors. We are asking AI companies to provide better credit when they are using our work. We should lead by example, and reflect on how good we are at giving credit to partners in the knowledge ecosystem. Don’t do the minimum required but do as much as possible to help them thrive. I invite you to join the conversation.

title: I Came for the Learning, Left with a Renewed Purpose: My Transformative Afroyanga Bootcamp 3.0 Experience
content:
Some experiences stay with you long after the event has ended. They are not just about the knowledge acquired or the activities undertaken; they are about the people you meet, the connections you build, the ideas you exchange, and the renewed sense of purpose you take home. For me, Afroyanga Bootcamp 3.0 was one of such experiences.

Organised by African & Proud, under the leadership of its co-founders, Richard Edozie and Kolawole Oyewole, Afroyanga Bootcamp 3.0 brought together young people, passionate Wikimedians, knowledge enthusiasts, and emerging changemakers in Lagos, Nigeria, for an enriching experience centred on open knowledge, leadership, collaboration, and capacity development.

Having participated in Afroyanga Bootcamp 2.0, returning for the third edition was particularly exciting. It was another opportunity to reconnect with the Afroyanga experience, meet new people, share experiences, and continue growing within a community that inspires young Africans to contribute meaningfully to the knowledge ecosystem.

title: Shine Her Light : Three Years of Unearthing African Women’s Stories and Creating Pathways for Visibility Empowerment and Change
content:
Across Africa, women have played significant roles in governance, research, education, entrepreneurship, civil society and community development. Yet many of their contributions remain inadequately documented and, consequently, difficult to discover within the digital public record.

This gap in documentation has implications beyond historical representation. When the contributions of African women are absent or under-represented online, students, researchers, journalists, policymakers and younger generations have limited access to reliable information about the women who have contributed to shaping their societies.

title: When does difficult behaviour become a UCoC concern?
content:
During a Wikimedia workshop, an experienced contributor repeatedly interrupts a newbie and dismisses their questions. Later, the newbie privately tells the facilitator that they no longer feel comfortable participating. What should the organiser do?

This was one of the situations explored during the EduWiki x VSN Workshop, Creating Safer and More Inclusive Wikimedia Spaces: Understanding and Applying the Universal Code of Conduct. Held on 15 October 2026, the online session brought together 56 participants from Central & Eastern Europe & Central Asia (CEECA), East, Southeast Asia and the Pacific (ESEAP), Middle East and North Africa (MENA), North America (NA), Northern and Western Europe (NWE), South Asia (SA) and the Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) regions, and was organised by the EduWiki Hub in collaboration with the Volunteer Supporters Network (VSN) and the Wikimedia Foundation’s Universal Code of Conduct Coordinating Committee (U4C).

The workshop looked at how the Universal Code of Conduct (UCoC) applies to Wikimedia projects, events, education programmes and community spaces, with practical discussions about recognising concerning behaviour and deciding how to respond.

title: Albanian Translation of the EduWiki Hub Starter Kit now available.
content:
The EduWiki Hub’s Newcomer’s Starter Kit, a comprehensive guide for integrating Wikimedia projects into education, is now available in Albanian. This translation was made possible by Vjollca Merdani, an educator, project manager, and active contributor to the Albanian Wikimedia community for over five years. With her extensive background in running educational programs and leading open knowledge initiatives, her translation brings this vital resource directly to Albanian speakers worldwide.

  • Clear, sequential instructions to help new volunteers and teachers bring Wikipedia into their lessons.
  • Action-oriented tools that help organizers build educational programs, run workshops, establish goals, and follow community guidelines.
  • Ideas, practical samples, and ready made exercises for coordinators working to create friendly, safe, and supportive environments for new members.
  • Community focused development created by participants to strengthen free learning through Wikimedia projects.

title: Empowering Free Knowledge: Highlights from WikiCamp Morocco 2026 in Marrakech
content:
The Wikimedia Morocco User Group held its fourth annual event, “WikiCamp Morocco 2026,” in Marrakech from October 19 to 21, 2026. The theme was “From Contribution to Initiative; Let us Build Our Organizational Team Together.” Active members met to improve their skills in creating free online content, documenting languages, leading groups, and organizing local projects.

Building on past events, this year focused on hands-on practice, better time management, and clear results. The goal was to help members move from working alone to leading organized, lasting projects across Morocco.

The program covered many topics. Attendees reviewed past activities and checked on programs like “Wikipedia in the Classroom” and “Ambassadors of Free Knowledge.” They also looked at Moroccan Darija and Amazigh Wikipedia projects, held contests, learned about technical tools, and discussed new ideas needing volunteer help.

To help preserve local speech, a hands-on workshop focused on Moroccan Darija Wikipedia. Participants recorded local words, meanings, example sentences, and audio clips to save rare regional vocabulary for future generations.

title: Books for Bassam, on the occasion of the 12th anniversary of Wikimedia Côte d’Ivoire’s affiliation
content:
Every year, since its 10 years of affiliation with the Wikimedia Foundation, Wikimedia Ivory Coast celebrates its anniversary by giving. In 2024, for the first edition of this initiative, the association supports a center for social integration. In 2025, an orphanage. In 2026, for the third year in a row, Wikimedia Côte d’Ivoire is collecting books, educational games and materials for an Ivorian library that has suffered damage. And your support makes a difference!

Bassam, the choice for Wikimedia Côte d’Ivoire’s 2026 community service. The seaside town of Bassam (Grand-Bassam) is home to a Wikimedia Côte d’Ivoire club, known as WikiClub Grand-Bassam.

In June 2026, heavy rains flooded the library at the Raffaelo Masto Cultural Center, located within the Carrefour Jeunesse in Grand-Bassam. Established by the Communauté Abel, the library was open to everyone — from students to parents. It also offered young people and adults a range of activities and a pathway toward social and professional integration, providing educational support and promoting African literature.

title: Bringing Climate Education to All: Empowering Students with Disabilities Through Open Knowledge
content:
On June 20, 2025, a dedicated team from the Eco Warriors Movement, in collaboration with the Environmental Science Students’ Association at Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST), visited the Ashanti School for the Deaf in Ghana. Our goal was simple yet profound: to conduct inclusive climate awareness training for students with hearing and visual impairments while supporting the school community with essential supplies.

This initiative is a core milestone of the project “Expanding Open Climate Education to Schools for Persons with Disabilities.” Supported by Creative Commons and executed in alignment with broader open knowledge principles alongside partners like Open Foundation West Africa and the Wikimedia Foundation, the project demonstrates how open educational resources (OER) and offline open technology can drive knowledge equity for underrepresented groups.

During the outreach, we engaged over 180 junior high and upper primary students, alongside seven staff members, including the Assistant Headmaster, Mr. Richard. Together, we explored urgent global and local environmental challenges, including:

title: EduWiki at LDC 2026: Can Wikimedia Education Reach Learners in Every Language?
content:
Language shapes who gets to participate in Wikimedia education. It influences whether educators can find useful learning materials, whether smaller language communities receive the support they need, and whether Wikimedia education programmes can be adapted to local contexts.

On 4 October 2026, Barakat Adegboye facilitated a workshop on behalf of EduWiki Hub at the Language Diversity Conference in Ghana. Titled Between Language and Access: Rethinking Wikimedia in Education for Underrepresented Languages, the session brought together 30 participants to explore these questions.

The session opened with a quick icebreaker. Participants were given a page from the Albanian translation of the EduWiki Newcomer’s Starter Kit and invited to look for specific words. It was a fun way to get everyone involved while introducing the idea that language can shape access to information and learning resources.

title: Creating Safer and Resilient Spaces: The Community Safety Toolkit by Wikimedia Deutschland
content:
For Wikimedia Deutschland (WMDE), community safety is not about having the perfect plan for when something goes wrong. It is about building the skills, knowledge and confidence to act before, during and after challenging situations. Over the past years, WMDE has worked with volunteers, communities and affiliates on questions around awareness, safety and psychosocial support. We wanted to make that experience easier to share and use.

The result is the WMDE Community Safety Toolkit: a collection of practical resources designed for chapters, affiliates and Wikimedia communities who want to make their own events and interactions safer in ways that fit their context, capacity and needs. The Toolkit was developed by WMDE’s Team Support & Consultancy. It is not an official Wikimedia Foundation standard: we share what works for us.

title: Wikimedia Foundation Bulletin 2026 Issue 21
content:
Here is a quick overview of highlights from the Wikimedia Foundation since our last issue on October 24. Previous editions of this bulletin are on Meta. Let foundationbulletin@wikimedia.org know if you have any feedback or suggestions for improvement!

  • Joy of contributing: The different ways in which joy shows up across Wikimedia movement: from music, sweets and weddings to Baby Globe.
  • Protecting open knowledge: The Wikimedia Foundation has filed an amicus brief to protect open knowledge in a major copyright case involving OpenAI and Microsoft.
  • Security update: Many Wikimedia tools were taken offline because of a security vulnerability in PHP. This affected many websites worldwide. Toolforge and Cloud VPS have been back up since October 22. Many important tools have been gradually restored. Some tools need the respective volunteer maintainers to restart them. Follow the work on Wikitech.
